anomalies.title: Anomalously large size / interstellar mass budget
anomalies.observation: Early photometry made 3I/ATLAS far brighter than expected for an interstellar object at ~4.5 AU: if the light came from a bare nucleus (albedo ~0.05), its radius would be ~10 km (~20 km diameter) — a mass Loeb put at roughly a million times 'Oumuamua's and a thousand times Borisov's (his July paper says over ten-million-fold and hundred-thousand-fold vs Borisov's core). Later HST/JWST work capped the nucleus far smaller (Jewitt et al. HST: radius ~0.22-2.8 km; Loeb's final essay uses a 2.6 km diameter). A separate September 2025 Loeb-Cloete-Veres analysis claimed the absence of pre-perihelion non-gravitational acceleration independently forced a mass above ~33 billion tons (diameter >5 km).
anomalies.loeb_take: Loeb (arXiv:2507.05881, submitted 2025-07-08) argued the interstellar rocky-material reservoir cannot deliver ~20-km objects at this detection rate — one would expect millions of 'Oumuamua-sized objects for each object of 3I/ATLAS's mass scale, so it is either a comet with a small core (<0.6 km) or a member of an implausibly rare population exceeding the interstellar mass budget. In his November 2025 likelihood ranking he assigned the mass anomaly P<0.001, and he kept the 'mass budget discrepancy' as anomaly #1 of his final 22-item list, arguing planetary-disk reservoirs miss the required mass by orders of magnitude even for the revised 2.6-km diameter.
anomalies.official_explanation: The brightness is dominated by a dust coma, not the nucleus; Hubble imaging (Jewitt et al., Aug 2025, arXiv:2508.02934) constrained the nucleus radius to <2.8 km (albedo 0.04, lower bound ~0.22 km), eliminating the population problem. Kilometer-scale interstellar comets are consistent with expected ISO size distributions, and Rubin Observatory is expected to find many more. Jason Wright (AstroWright) notes Loeb's later 33-billion-ton mass floor rested on assuming non-gravitational-acceleration measurement precision of 1e-10 AU/day^2 when the actual precision is ~1e-7 — off by ~1000x.
anomalies.loeb_quote: [paraphrase] The inferred nucleus diameter of 2.6 kilometers and the number density of its parent population (assuming a natural comet) exceed the mass reservoir of planetary disks around low-metallicity stars by orders of magnitude.
anomalies._verifyNotes: Two fixes, rest confirmed. (1) CONFLATION: the "~33 billion tons" mass was wrongly paired with the July ~20-km bare-nucleus inference. 33 billion tons (3.3e13 kg, with diameter >5 km) is the lower bound from a separate September 2025 Loeb-Cloete-Veres claim that 3I/ATLAS showed no pre-perihelion non-gravitational acceleration — the very claim Jason Wright showed rested on assuming measurement precision of 1e-10 AU/day^2 when actual precision is ~1e-7 (off ~1000x). The July 8 arXiv paper (2507.05881) instead argued a ~10 km radius (albedo 0.05) implying mass "over ten million times" 'Oumuamua's and "at least a hundred thousand times" Borisov's core (publicly framed by Loeb as "a million times 'Oumuamua, a thousand times Borisov"), and that "one would expect millions of objects like 'Oumuamua for each object on the mass scale of 3I/ATLAS." (2) MISATTRIBUTION: P<0.001 was not assigned in the July arXiv paper; Loeb assigned P<0.001 to the mass anomaly in his November 2025 Medium essay "Anomalies of 3I/ATLAS, Organized by Likelihood." Confirmed: date 2025-07-08 matches arXiv:2507.05881 v1; Jewitt et al. HST (arXiv:2508.02934, Aug 2025) nucleus radius <2.8 km (albedo 0.04), lower bound ~0.22 km if CO-driven; Loeb's final 22-anomaly essay lists the mass-budget discrepancy as anomaly #1 using a 2.6-km nucleus diameter and "orders of magnitude" reservoir shortfall; official explanation (dust-coma-dominated brightness, km-scale nucleus consistent with ISO size distribution, Rubin expected to find more) is fairly stated. Added a [paraphrase]-flagged quote of anomaly #1 wording and primary-source URLs.

anomalies.title: Ecliptic-plane alignment (~5 deg, 0.2%)
anomalies.observation: 3I/ATLAS's retrograde hyperbolic trajectory (inclination ~175 deg) lies within about 5 degrees of the ecliptic — the orbital plane of the planets. For a randomly oriented incoming interstellar trajectory, Loeb computed a ~0.2% chance of such alignment.
anomalies.loeb_take: In the July 2025 paper 'Is the Interstellar Object 3I/ATLAS Alien Technology?' (Hibberd, Crowl, Loeb; arXiv v1 submitted July 16, 2025), this was the founding anomaly: a low retrograde tilt to the ecliptic 'offers various benefits to an Extra-terrestrial Intelligence,' making the path look like a designed reconnaissance trajectory with optimal access to the inner planets. After introducing the Loeb scale in August 2025 (arXiv:2508.09167), Loeb kept this among the core set anchoring his rating — 'there are eight anomalies that endow it with a rank of 4 on the Loeb scale.'
anomalies.official_explanation: Mainstream astronomers call this a textbook a-posteriori probability fallacy: the specific property was chosen after observing it ('he chose specific aspects of the comet's orbit to compute probabilities for after he knew what they were' — Jason Wright), and with any object some ~0.2%-level coincidences are guaranteed among the many orbital parameters one could examine. AstroWright (Nov 9, 2025) labels it a 'classic fallacy and misuse of probability theory,' citing Hector Socas-Navarro's detailed critique; there is also mild survey selection bias toward ecliptic discoveries. Dynamically the orbit is unremarkable for a galactic-disk object.
anomalies.loeb_quote: aligned to within 5 degrees with the orbital plane of the planets
anomalies.quote_source: '3I/ATLAS is Fading Away, Leaving Us to Ponder Over Its 22 Mysterious Anomalies', Medium, March 12, 2026
anomalies._verifyNotes: Core facts all check out: arXiv v1 of Hibberd/Crowl/Loeb was submitted exactly 2025-07-16; the 5-degree / 0.2% figures are real (and distinct from the paper's separate 0.005% planet-close-approach figure); the loeb_quote is verified verbatim in the March 12, 2026 Medium essay cited; the AstroWright post exists (Nov 9, 2025, Jason T. Wright). Two fixes: (1) official_explanation quoted Wright as 'classic misuse of probability theory' — his exact wording is 'classic fallacy and misuse of probability theory'; corrected to exact quote and added his a-posteriori elaboration. (2) loeb_take implied the rank-of-4 / '8 anomalies' statement came from the July 2025 paper; the Loeb scale was actually introduced in his August 2025 paper (arXiv:2508.09167) and the verified sentence 'there are eight anomalies that endow it with a rank of 4 on the Loeb scale' comes from later Medium posts. Reworded to keep the July paper as the founding-anomaly source without misattributing the scale ranking to it; added the Loeb-scale paper to sources.

anomalies.title: Fine-tuned arrival geometry (Mars/Venus/Jupiter passes)
anomalies.observation: The arrival time placed 3I/ATLAS within tens of millions of km of three planets: ~29 million km (0.19 AU) from Mars on Oct 3, 2025, ~0.65 AU from Venus in November, and 53.6 million km (0.358 AU) from Jupiter on Mar 16, 2026. Loeb estimated a combined probability of order 0.005% (he later listed P=0.00005) for a random interstellar object to thread this sequence.
anomalies.loeb_take: In the July 2025 paper and later essays, Loeb argued the timing looks 'fine-tuned' for planetary reconnaissance — exactly the flyby program a probe designer would choose. This was one of the original 8 anomalies behind his rank-4 assignment and remained #3 in his final 22-item list.
anomalies.official_explanation: Astronomers respond that any object traveling in the ecliptic plane will necessarily pass 'near' planets, so the claim double-counts the ecliptic-alignment anomaly; AstroWright calls it question-begging, noting Loeb treats both close approaches and non-close approaches as anomalous. Tens of millions of km are distant passes with no operational significance. NASA states all evidence points to a natural comet.
anomalies._verifyNotes: none — all facts verified against primary sources. Date: arXiv:2507.12213 (Hibberd, Crowl, Loeb) submitted 2025-07-16; abstract states 3I/ATLAS "approaches surprisingly close to Venus, Mars and Jupiter, with a probability of <~0.005%". Distances: Mars 0.194 AU (~29M km) on 2025-10-03; Venus 0.65 AU on 2025-11-03; Jupiter 53.56+/-0.45M km (0.358+/-0.003 AU) on 2026-03-16 — all match the entry. The P=0.00005 figure appears in Loeb's Nov 23, 2025 "Anomalies of 3I/ATLAS, Organized by Likelihood" essay and is the same value as 0.005% (fraction vs percent), so the parenthetical is accurate though a reader could misread it as a revised smaller number. Item is #3 in Loeb's 22-anomaly list (exact wording: "The arrival time of 3I/ATLAS was fine-tuned to bring it to minimum distances of 29 and 54 million kilometers from Mars and Jupiter, respectively, and be unobservable from Earth at perihelion"). Loeb's on-record statement "there are eight anomalies that endow it with a rank of 4 on the Loeb scale" supports the loeb_take. Wright's Nov 9, 2025 AstroWright post verbatim: "Claiming the arrival was 'fine tuned' is classic question begging" and "Close, not close, both anomalous!", citing Steve Desch that a comet in the ecliptic unsurprisingly passes near some planets — the official_explanation is a fair rendering. loeb_quote is empty, so no quote-verification issue. All three source URLs are real and on-topic.

anomalies.title: Perihelion hidden behind the Sun
anomalies.observation: Perihelion occurred Oct 29, 2025 (Oct 29-30 across time zones) at 1.356 AU while 3I/ATLAS was on the far side of the Sun as seen from Earth (solar conjunction Oct 21) — unobservable by ground-based telescopes from late September until it re-emerged in early December 2025.
anomalies.loeb_take: In the July 16, 2025 arXiv paper (Hibberd, Crowl & Loeb, arXiv:2507.12213), Loeb and coauthors flagged that this geometry would let a technological probe execute a clandestine reverse Solar Oberth maneuver — an optimal braking burn at maximum solar depth — while hidden from Earth. In his ranked anomaly lists this is folded into the 'fine-tuned arrival time' anomaly (P=0.00005, Nov 23, 2025 Medium list), and he explicitly called for post-conjunction astrometry to check for maneuvers.
anomalies.official_explanation: Perihelion viewing geometry is set by chance orbital phase; solar conjunctions like this are routine for comets. Moreover the object was NOT unobserved: STEREO (Sep 11-Oct 2), SOHO/LASCO (Oct 16-26), GOES-19 CCOR-1, PUNCH, and Parker Solar Probe's WISPR (Oct 15-Nov 5) imaged it through conjunction and perihelion, Mars orbiters (MRO/HiRISE, ExoMars TGO) imaged it at the ~Oct 3 Mars flyby, and Europa Clipper observed it Nov 6. It re-emerged on a trajectory consistent with a natural comet; the small (~3.7-sigma) non-gravitational acceleration reported by JPL/MPC is attributed by most astronomers to ordinary cometary outgassing.
anomalies.loeb_quote: The eclipse by the Sun from Earth of 3I/ATLAS at perihelion, would allow it to conduct a clandestine reverse Solar Oberth Manoeuvre, an optimal high-thrust strategy for interstellar spacecraft to brake and stay bound to the Sun.
anomalies.quote_source: Hibberd, Crowl & Loeb, 'Is the Interstellar Object 3I/ATLAS Alien Technology?', arXiv:2507.12213 (submitted Jul 16, 2025)
anomalies._verifyNotes: Core anomaly is real and date is exact (arXiv:2507.12213 v1 submitted 2025-07-16). Fixes: (1) Oberth claim refined — the Hibberd/Crowl/Loeb paper describes a clandestine REVERSE Solar Oberth maneuver to brake and stay bound to the Sun, not merely a 'course change'; added the verified exact quote and attribution (paper is co-authored, not Loeb alone). (2) 'Final list' softened to 'ranked anomaly lists' — the folding into the fine-tuned-arrival anomaly (P=0.00005, incl. 'be unobservable from Earth at perihelion') is verified in his Nov 23, 2025 'Anomalies of 3I/ATLAS, Organized by Likelihood' (15 anomalies); his last list had 22. (3) Official explanation: removed unverified 'roughly half of comets are poorly placed' statistic; corrected spacecraft list and dates (STEREO Sep 11–Oct 2; SOHO/LASCO Oct 16–26; GOES-19 CCOR-1; PUNCH; Parker Solar Probe WISPR Oct 15–Nov 5; Mars orbiters MRO/HiRISE and ExoMars TGO at the ~Oct 3 Mars flyby; Europa Clipper Nov 6); reworded 'emerged on the predicted natural-comet trajectory' to acknowledge the reported ~3.7-sigma non-gravitational acceleration that mainstream astronomers attribute to normal cometary outgassing. (4) Noted ground observability resumed early December 2025 (conjunction from late September). Perihelion Oct 29, 2025 at ~1.356 AU confirmed.

anomalies.title: Sunward anti-tail / collimated sunward jet
anomalies.observation: The Hubble image of July 21, 2025 showed the dust distribution extended toward the Sun, about ten times longer than wide, with no classical dust tail; a sunward anti-tail re-appeared in July-August and again in November 2025, eventually reaching ~1 million km. Mars HiRISE imaging on Oct 2, 2025 also showed a glowing extension ahead of the object along its direction of motion.
anomalies.loeb_take: Loeb argued this is a genuine sunward-pointing jet, not the perspective illusion seen in thousands of normal comets (P<0.001 in his Nov 23, 2025 likelihood-ordered list), and that sustaining a collimated sunward plume is more naturally explained by a thruster pointed at the Sun for braking than by sublimating ice.
anomalies.official_explanation: Anti-tails and sunward fans are well-documented comet phenomena; Jewitt's HST modeling explains the geometry with large, slow-moving dust grains ejected from the sunlit hemisphere that lag the nucleus, combined with projection effects. AstroWright notes the underlying mechanism has been understood for ~50 years and similar features appear in comets like 17P/Holmes and C/2016 R2.
anomalies._verifyNotes: none — all claims verified against primary sources. Hubble image date (July 21, 2025), ~10x elongation (Loeb deprojects to ~11.6x), anti-tail in July-August and November 2025, ~1 million km sunward jet extent (0.95M km measured Nov 9, 2025), HiRISE Oct 2, 2025 direction-of-motion extension, P<0.001 in Loeb's Nov 23, 2025 likelihood-ordered list, Jewitt & Luu's large-slow-grain HST model (100 um grains at ~5 m/s from sunlit hemisphere), and Wright's Nov 9, 2025 AstroWright post citing Sekanina 1974 ("understood for 50 years") with 17P/Holmes and C/2016 R2 examples are all accurate. Loeb quote field is empty so no wording to verify; loeb_take is a fair paraphrase of his published thruster-braking speculation. Optional (not applied): could add Loeb's "Remarkable Large-Scale Structure of Anti-Tail and Tail Jets" Medium essay as the direct source for the ~1 million km figure.

anomalies.title: CO2-dominated coma; water only ~4% of plume
anomalies.observation: JWST NIRSpec observations of Aug 6, 2025 at 3.32 AU (Cordiner et al., arXiv:2508.18209) found a carbon-dioxide-dominated gas coma with CO2/H2O = 7.6 +/- 0.3 (~8:1) — among the highest ratios ever observed in any comet, ~4.5 sigma above the trend for solar-system comets (survey median ~0.12). By mass the plume was ~87% CO2, ~9% CO, and only ~4% water.
anomalies.loeb_take: Loeb listed the near-absence of water — the defining volatile of familiar comets — as a minor anomaly at P<0.1 in his 13-item likelihood-ranked list (Nov 23, 2025), suggesting the 'gas plume' might not be cometary sublimation at all but sunlight releasing ices and dust accumulated on the surface of a technological object during its interstellar journey. It is not a separate item in his final 22-anomaly list (Mar 12, 2026), compiled after post-perihelion water detections.
anomalies.official_explanation: A CO2-rich nucleus is natural for a body formed near its parent disk's CO2 snowline or processed by galactic cosmic rays over billions of years (arXiv:2510.26308); at >3 AU water sublimates inefficiently while CO2 vents freely. Water/OH production rose strongly closer to the Sun — MeerKAT detected 1665/1667 MHz OH absorption on Oct 24, 2025 (ATel #17473), and SOHO/SWAN measured ~3.2e29 water molecules/s near perihelion — and interstellar comets are expected to show compositional diversity.
anomalies.loeb_quote: The gas plume surrounding 3I/ATLAS contains only 4% water by mass, a dominant constituent of familiar solar-system comets.
anomalies._verifyNotes: Entry is substantively accurate; three fixes: (1) "the highest ratio ever measured in any comet" overstates the paper — Cordiner et al. say CO2/H2O = 7.6 +/- 0.3 is "among the highest ever observed in a comet" (4.5 sigma above the solar-system trend confirmed). Title/observation wording softened accordingly. (2) The claim that the anomaly appeared in Loeb's 15-item list (Dec 18, 2025) could not be verified; verified facts are: it appears as a minor anomaly at P<0.1 in his 13-item likelihood-ranked list (Medium, Nov 23, 2025) and is NOT a separate item in his final 22-anomaly list (Medium, Mar 12, 2026). The unverified 15-list claim was removed. (3) Added a verified Loeb quote from the Nov 23, 2025 Medium post ("The gas plume surrounding 3I/ATLAS contains only 4% water by mass, a dominant constituent of familiar solar-system comets."). All other facts confirmed: obs date UT 2025-08-06 at rh ~3.32 AU, arXiv submission 2025-08-25, mass split 87% CO2 / 9% CO / ~4% H2O, official explanation real and fairly stated (cosmic-ray processing paper arXiv:2510.26308; MeerKAT 1665/1667 MHz OH absorption detected Oct 24, 2025, ATel #17473; post-perihelion SOHO/SWAN water production ~3.17e29 molecules/s on Nov 6, 2025).

anomalies.title: Nickel emission without iron (nickel-carbonyl signature)
anomalies.observation: VLT/UVES spectroscopy (early Jul-Aug 21, 2025; ~4.4 to 2.85 AU inbound) detected strong atomic nickel (Ni I) emission with iron (Fe I) undetected — by Aug 21 the Ni production rate was 4.6 +/- 0.7 g/s versus CN at 17.6 +/- 2.0 g/s, rising steeply (Q(Ni) proportional to r^-7.7). Keck II/KCWI imaging (Aug 24, published Oct 2025) confirmed the Ni is concentrated within ~600 km of the nucleus (e-folding radius 593.7 +/- 14.8 km vs 841 km for CN). The Ni/CN ratio (~0.1) is orders of magnitude above the solar-system comet median and higher than 2I/Borisov.
anomalies.loeb_take: Loeb stressed that release of nickel without iron matches the industrial nickel-refining process via nickel tetracarbonyl, Ni(CO)4 — writing that nickel without iron 'is a signature of industrial production of nickel alloys' and that the carbonyl channel is 'an extremely rare and exotic possibility in comets, whereas it is a standard technology for industrial nickel refining.'
anomalies.official_explanation: Ni and Fe emission had already been detected together (at roughly equal abundance) in ~20 solar-system comets and in 2I/Borisov (Manfroid et al. 2021), with low-temperature carbonyl/metal-organic sublimation a leading natural mechanism. For 3I/ATLAS, the observing teams themselves proposed natural in-situ Ni(CO)4 (or Ni-organic/PAH complex) formation and photodissociation near the nucleus — which predicts exactly the observed central concentration — with Fe carbonyl being less volatile and Fe I lines harder to excite/detect at large distances. Fe was subsequently detected as 3I/ATLAS approached the Sun (arXiv 2509.26053), and the Ni/Fe ratio dropped rapidly with decreasing heliocentric distance, trending toward normal comet values. Astronomers (e.g. Jason Wright) call it an extreme but chemically explicable value, not evidence of artificial nickel plating.
anomalies.loeb_quote: is a signature of industrial production of nickel alloys
anomalies.quote_source: Avi Loeb, 'A Steeply-Rising Production of Cyanide and Nickel Without Iron in the Gas Plume Around 3I/ATLAS', Medium, Aug 28, 2025 (verified)
anomalies._verifyNotes: 1) Date confirmed: Loeb's nickel-without-iron Medium essay published 2025-08-28. 2) Ni 4.6+/-0.7 g/s and CN 17.6+/-2.0 g/s are real but are the VLT (UVES) rates as of Aug 21, 2025 (arXiv 2508.18382), not Keck; Keck KCWI (Aug 24, arXiv 2510.11779) measured lower rates (~0.9 g/s Ni, Q(CN)=(9.1+/-0.4)e22/s ~3.9 g/s) and the ~600 km concentration (Ni e-folding radius 593.7+/-14.8 km). Ni/CN ~0.1 is orders of magnitude above the solar-system comet median but only modestly higher than 2I/Borisov. 3) "P<0.001" is invented — no probability appears in either Loeb essay; removed. 4) Quote "observed only in human industrial processes" not verifiable; replaced with verified Loeb wording "Nickel without iron is a signature of industrial production of nickel alloys" (Aug 28, 2025 essay). 5) Official explanation was wrong in claiming Ni-without-Fe was previously measured in many comets and Borisov — those objects showed Ni AND Fe together at roughly equal abundance (Manfroid et al. 2021); corrected to note the observing teams proposed natural carbonyl/metal-organic chemistry, and that Fe was later detected in 3I/ATLAS (arXiv 2509.26053) with Ni/Fe falling rapidly toward perihelion. Jason Wright rebuttal source verified real.

anomalies.title: Extreme negative polarization
anomalies.observation: Pre-perihelion polarimetry with FORS2/VLT, ALFOSC/NOT and FoReRo2 (phase angles 7.7-22.4 deg) revealed an unprecedentedly deep, narrow negative polarization branch: minimum -2.7% at 7 deg phase angle with an inversion angle of ~17 deg — a combination never seen in any asteroid or comet, including 2I/Borisov (arXiv:2509.05181, Sept 5, 2025).
anomalies.loeb_take: Loeb listed this at P<0.01 as a medium anomaly: light-scattering behavior unprecedented among all known comets, possibly related to the anomalous sunward anti-tail, and another entry in a chain of coincidences whose combined probability he multiplied to argue 3I/ATLAS is 'extremely rare and mysterious'. It stayed as #21 in his final 22-item list.
anomalies.official_explanation: The measuring team's own conclusion is natural: the polarization is extreme but continuous with behavior of trans-Neptunian objects and Centaur Pholus, implying fine, possibly water-ice-bearing aggregate dust — evidence 3I is a distinct type of comet, expanding known diversity. AstroWright: negative polarization itself is normal for comets; this is just a stronger case, and no one has proposed why a spacecraft would produce it.
anomalies._verifyNotes: none — every checkable claim verified against primary sources. Date matches arXiv:2509.05181 submission (Sept 5, 2025; Loeb responded Sept 10). Instruments, phase-angle range 7.7-22.4 deg, minimum -2.7% at 7 deg, and ~17 deg inversion angle all match the paper abstract verbatim. Loeb's P<0.01 "medium anomaly" classification and the multiplied-probabilities / "extremely rare and mysterious" phrasing are verified in his Nov 23, 2025 post "Anomalies of 3I/ATLAS, Organized by Likelihood"; the #21-of-22 ranking is verified in his Mar 12, 2026 post "3I/ATLAS is Fading Away, Leaving Us to Ponder Over Its 22 Mysterious Anomalies" (still his most current comprehensive list as of mid-2026), which also confirms the anti-tail linkage. Official explanation fairly represents both the measuring team's conclusion (continuity with TNOs/Centaur Pholus, fine possibly water-ice-bearing dust, new class of small bodies) and Wright's Nov 9, 2025 AstroWright counterpoint. Optional enhancement (not a correction): loeb_quote could be filled with the verified sentence "3I/ATLAS shows extreme negative polarization, unprecedented for all known comets, including 2I/Borisov. This unusual polarization may be related to its unusual anti-tail." sourced to the Mar 12, 2026 Medium post.

anomalies.title: Arrival direction matches the 1977 Wow! Signal
anomalies.observation: Loeb noted that 3I/ATLAS's back-traced position in mid-August 1977 (RA 19h40m = 295 deg, Dec -19 deg) lies ~4 deg in RA and 8 deg in Dec (~9 deg total) from the direction of the famous narrowband 'Wow! Signal' detected by Ohio State's Big Ear telescope on Aug 15, 1977 (RA 19h25m = 291 deg, Dec -27 deg). He put the chance of two random sky directions aligning that closely at ~0.6% (P=0.006).
anomalies.loeb_take: In 'Was the Wow! Signal Emitted from 3I/ATLAS?' (Medium, Sept 28, 2025) Loeb speculated the 1977 signal could have been radio emission from 3I/ATLAS itself, calculating that a transmitter at its then-distance of ~600 AU would have needed 0.5-2 gigawatts — 'the output of a typical nuclear reactor on Earth.' He kept the directional coincidence as anomaly #12 of his final 22-item list (March 12, 2026): arrival 'coincident with the radio Wow! Signal to within 9 degrees, with a probability of 0.6%.'
anomalies.official_explanation: Critics note 9 degrees is enormous in radio-astronomy terms — many times the Big Ear beam size. Penn State's Jason Wright (AstroWright, Nov 9, 2025) wrote '9 degrees from the Wow! Signal is a long way away!... it very definitely did not come from the direction of the Wow! Signal,' calling the anomaly 'ridiculous.' In 1977 the object was ~600 AU away with no plausible natural emission mechanism, and the Wow! Signal itself is widely attributed to terrestrial interference or a transient natural hydrogen-line source (e.g., Abel Mendez's cold hydrogen cloud hypothesis).
anomalies.loeb_quote: The chance of two random directions in the sky being aligned to that level is about 0.6 percent.
anomalies.quote_source: Avi Loeb, 'Was the Wow! Signal Emitted from 3I/ATLAS?', Medium, Sept 28, 2025

anomalies.title: Non-gravitational acceleration at perihelion
anomalies.observation: JPL's post-perihelion orbit solution (Davide Farnocchia, Oct 30, 2025) required a radial non-gravitational acceleration with A1 ~ 1.6e-6 AU/day^2 normalized at 1 AU — equivalent to a radial acceleration of ~135 km/day^2 (~9e-7 AU/day^2) at the 1.36 AU perihelion distance, plus a transverse component of ~60 km/day^2. As the data arc grew the coefficient dropped: ~4e-7 AU/day^2 by Nov 24, then ~6.8e-8 AU/day^2 under a 1/r^2 (CO2-sublimation) model. In 2026 Loeb continued the thread, arguing (Mar 2026) the acceleration is not directed purely away from the Sun and linking it (Apr 2026) to the object's three-jet system.
anomalies.loeb_take: In 'First Evidence for a Non-Gravitational Acceleration of 3I/ATLAS at Perihelion' and 'Afterthoughts...' (both Oct 31, 2025), Loeb calculated that producing the initial acceleration by rocket-effect outgassing would require 3I/ATLAS to shed on the order of a tenth to a sixth of its mass near perihelion (his figure quoted as ~13% in critiques) — at least 5.5 billion tons from a >=33-billion-ton nucleus — which should have produced a massive observable gas cloud by December. Absent that cloud, he argued, the acceleration 'might be regarded as a technological signature' of an internal propulsion system.
anomalies.official_explanation: Non-gravitational accelerations are standard comet behavior; the measured value shrank more than 20-fold as more astrometry accumulated, and the final magnitude is consistent with ordinary volatile outgassing (arXiv:2511.07450 finds CO-driven outgassing reproduces it with no exotic volatiles needed). Early solutions were inflated by systematic astrometric biases — ~0.5 arcsec tailward coma-photocenter offsets and the October solar-conjunction data gap (arXiv:2603.00782) — and Jason Wright noted that even 13% mass loss near perihelion 'is hardly weird' for a comet.
anomalies.loeb_quote: If we do not observe a massive cloud of gas around 3I/ATLAS in December, then the reported non-gravitational acceleration near perihelion might be regarded as a technological signature.
anomalies._verifyNotes: The anomaly is real and the core JPL numbers (A1 1.6e-6 -> 4e-7 -> 6.8e-8 AU/day^2) are confirmed, but four fixes were needed. (1) Date: Loeb's 'First Evidence' post published Oct 31, 2025 (JPL solution Oct 30), not Nov 5 — corrected to 2025-10-31. anomalies.title: Anomalous brightening and blue color at perihelion
anomalies.observation: Analysis of STEREO-A (SECCHI HI1/COR2), SOHO/LASCO C3 and GOES-19 CCOR-1 coronagraph imagery (Zhang, Lowell Observatory & Battams, NRL; arXiv:2510.25035, submitted Oct 28, 2025) showed 3I/ATLAS brightening near perihelion roughly as r^-7.5 (±1.0) — far steeper than typical comets (r^-2 to r^-4) — while its color turned bluer than the Sun, unusual because dust comae normally redden reflected sunlight.

In his Nov 23, 2025 likelihood ranking he placed it in his least-anomalous category at P<0.1: it 'brightened faster than any known comet' while bluer than sunlight, which he suggested might be 'a signature that its engine turned on' near perihelion rather than sunlight-driven sublimation. It appears as item #22 on his final 22-anomaly list (March 12, 2026).

Zhang & Battams themselves conclude the blue color is consistent with gas emission contributing a substantial fraction of the visible brightness. Fast-moving interstellar comets get less heating time inbound, so late, sharp activity onsets are expected.

anomalies.title: Extreme mass combined with extreme speed

The higher speed is separately explained by mainstream kinematics: 3I/ATLAS's velocity is consistent with an origin in the Galaxy's older, dynamically hotter thick-disk population, implying a kinematic age of ~7-10 Gyr — consistent with later isotope evidence of great age.

anomalies.title: Perijove distance equals Jupiter's Hill radius
anomalies.observation: The predicted minimum distance from Jupiter on Mar 16, 2026 — 53.445 +/- 0.06 million km — matched Jupiter's Hill radius (53.502 million km) to within one standard deviation, about one part in a thousand. Loeb put the probability of the coincidence at less than 0.00004 (about 1 in 26,000, scaled to Jupiter's orbital diameter) and noted the non-gravitational acceleration measured near perihelion shifted the perijove by ~0.1 million km — exactly the course correction needed to produce the match.
anomalies.loeb_take: In 'An Extraordinary New Anomaly of 3I/ATLAS' (Nov 22, 2025), Loeb argued a passage precisely at the Hill radius — where Jupiter's Lagrange points L1 and L2 sit — is where an artificial object could release technological devices into bound Jovian orbits with minimal fuel and orbital corrections, and suggested Juno or other human-made orbiters at Jupiter could search for new objects orbiting the planet.
anomalies.official_explanation: Astronomers called the statistics post-hoc numerology: astrophysicists including Scott Manley and David Kipping publicly flagged flaws in Loeb's probability analysis, and critics (e.g. Steve Desch, Jason Wright) noted such 'fine-tuning' probabilities are computed after the fact from one of many possible 'special' distances. The prediction itself dissolved: the actual March 16, 2026 pass occurred at 53.6 million km (0.358330 AU) — slightly outside the Hill radius — with ESA's JUICE observing an ordinary cometary coma with dust and ion tails, and no new satellites of Jupiter were reported.

(3) Probability: Loeb stated the likelihood as "smaller than 0.00004" (~1 in 26,000) scaled to Jupiter's orbital diameter, not a computed P=0.00004 — softened accordingly.

anomalies.title: Dust particle size paradox
anomalies.observation: Sustaining the ~400,000 km sunward anti-tail jet requires dust grains far larger than the sub-micron particles that dominate ordinary comet comae: Loeb brackets them between ~1 and ~100 microns (characteristic radius ~10 microns) — big enough to resist solar radiation pressure, small enough for gas drag to accelerate to jet speeds. Millimeter-scale or larger grains are excluded because the total ejected dust mass needed to produce the observed scattered sunlight would become implausibly large for the nucleus.
anomalies.loeb_take: Loeb kept this as anomaly #16 of his final 22-item list (Mar 12, 2026): the glow is dominated by particles much larger than common sub-micron interstellar dust, yet they cannot exceed millimeter size without mass-budget inconsistencies — an anomalous size bracket for a comet. From ~10-micron grains he estimated ~10 million kg of dust shed (~3.3 kg/s) and asked whether 3I/ATLAS accumulated such grains in a molecular cloud.
anomalies.official_explanation: Refereed HST analysis (Jewitt & Luu 2025, ApJL) self-consistently explains the sunward fan that evolved into an anti-sunward tail as large grains (~100 microns) ejected slowly (~5 m/s) — behavior well documented in low-activity and distantly active comets — and an MNRAS study of the physics of cometary anti-tails as observed in 3I/ATLAS reaches similar conclusions. Mass-loss estimates fit cometary norms once realistic size distributions (not single-size grains) are used; grain properties vary widely between comets and no paradox is recognized in the refereed literature.

Loeb's particle-size argument was published Dec 25, 2025 (Medium essay '3I/ATLAS Sheds Particles that Are Much Bigger Than Common Sunlight-Scattering Dust') with the mass estimate following Dec 26 ('The Dust Mass Shed by 3I/ATLAS'); his Nov 23, 2025 anomaly list did not yet include this item. Corrected to 2025-12-25. (2) NUMBERS: 'mm-scale or larger' inverts Loeb's claim. He argued grains must be >1 micron and <100 microns (characteristic ~10 microns) to sustain the ~400,000 km anti-tail; millimeter-or-larger grains are the case he EXCLUDED because they would require an untenable total dust mass to produce the observed scattered light. Total shed mass he estimated: ~10 million kg at ~3.3 kg/s (other essays cite 150-500 kg/s peak loss rates near perihelion, a separate figure). (3) LOEB_TAKE: '#16 of his final list' is CONFIRMED — the dust particle size paradox is item 16 of the 22-anomaly list in his Mar 12, 2026 essay '3I/ATLAS is Fading Away, Leaving Us to Ponder Over Its 22 Mysterious Anomalies.' anomalies.title: Rotation axis aligned with sunward direction
anomalies.observation: A wobbling high-latitude jet observed pre-perihelion (Serra-Ricart, Licandro & Alarcon, arXiv 2512.12819) yielded a spin-axis solution (sky-projected PA 280.7 deg, ~15.48 h rotation period). Loeb inferred from this geometry that the nucleus spin axis was aligned to within 8 degrees of the sunward direction as 3I/ATLAS entered the solar system, and put the probability of a random spin pole landing there at 0.5% (P=0.005). An earlier Loeb & Scarmato coma-morphology analysis had found a looser 10-20 degree alignment (1.5-6% probability).
anomalies.loeb_take: First flagged Dec 16, 2025 as the '14th anomaly'; it became anomaly #6 of the final 22. Loeb argued a sun-pointing spin axis gives the object a permanent dayside and nightside, and that if the antipodal jet geometry requires a second sublimating ice pocket placed near the opposite pole with similar precision, the improbability compounds multiplicatively to 0.005 x 0.005 = 2.5e-5 - fine-tuned orientation he suggests is more naturally read as a maintained attitude than a random tumble.
anomalies.official_explanation: Spin-pole solutions derived from fuzzy coma and jet features are highly model-dependent (Loeb's own earlier analysis gave 10-20 degrees, and independent coma-shape fits allowed two different poles), and seasonal activity biases naturally select for apparent sunward alignment since sun-facing active regions dominate observed morphology. A published natural mechanism also exists: torque from asymmetric ice sublimation can drive the spin axis toward the sunward direction, and a ~90-degree obliquity nucleus with a sun-pointed pole naturally explains dayside-dominant sublimation - no design implication required.

anomalies.title: Wobbling high-latitude sunward jet
anomalies.observation: A pre-perihelion study (arXiv:2512.12819, submitted 2025-12-14; Serra-Ricart, Licandro & Alarcon, A&A 705, L3) detected a faint high-latitude jet in the inner coma at PA 280±10 degrees across seven August 2025 nights, with a periodic 7.74±0.35 h modulation consistent with a high-latitude jet precessing around the nucleus spin axis (implied rotation period 15.48±0.70 h). Loeb argued the sunward wobble requires the jet's base to lie within 8 degrees of the sun-facing rotation pole, and assigned that pole-proximate location a probability of 0.5%.
anomalies.loeb_take: Anomaly #7 on his 22-anomaly list: the jet's base sits improbably close to the sun-facing pole (0.5%). Combined with the matching post-perihelion coincidence at the opposite pole (anomaly #8), he squares it: 0.5% x 0.5% = 0.000025 (2.5e-5) that sunward anti-tail jets appear both before and after perihelion by chance.

The 'independent' probabilities Loeb multiplies are not independent — they describe the same geometry.

anomalies.title: Jet base 'insulation' on the nightside
anomalies.observation: Because 3I/ATLAS's rotation axis is nearly aligned with the sunward direction, each anti-tail jet's launch base sits on the nightside for months at a stretch (the post-perihelion jet's base was on the nightside before perihelion, and vice versa), yet the jets are active only while their base faces the Sun.
anomalies.loeb_take: Anomaly #9 of Loeb's 22-item wrap-up list (March 2026; first argued as point #8 in his Dec 17, 2025 essay): for the bases to stay dormant through months of darkness they must be extremely well insulated, but heat should naturally conduct throughout a comet's body — so, per Loeb, the on/off pattern hints at engineered surfaces or controlled venting rather than passive ice.

Heat conduction through a porous nucleus is extremely inefficient, contradicting the premise that warmth should spread to the nightside; no exotic insulation is required. No agency-level rebuttal addresses this numbered claim specifically, but the underlying thermophysics is standard.

He also used the geometry constructively: a jet wobbling within an ~8-degree cone about a fixed spin axis could produce the sunward anti-tail before perihelion and a counter-jet after it.

The general response to Loeb's coincidence claims (e.g., Jason Wright's critiques of his fine-tuning statistics) applies: the two angles arise from unrelated physics — the 16-degree deflection is routine orbital mechanics for any body with that perihelion distance and speed, while the jet opening angle is a soft, method-dependent measurement — and comparing enough angle pairs post hoc guarantees some near-integer ratios.

anomalies.title: SPHEREx icy-grain signature disappearance

anomalies.title: Rare Sun-Earth axis alignment (Jan 22, 2026)
anomalies.observation: On Jan 22, 2026, 3I/ATLAS crossed the Sun-Earth axis at a phase angle of just 0.69 degrees (near-perfect opposition), with the phase angle below 2 degrees for about a week (Jan 19-26) and the anti-tail direction projected toward Earth at the moment of alignment.
anomalies.loeb_take: Loeb (with Mauro Barbieri, arXiv:2601.08624) announced the alignment on Jan 13, 2026 primarily as a 'narrow but well-defined observational window' to measure the opposition surge and probe whether the dust is pristine (fluffy fractal aggregates) or thermally processed; in his final March 2026 recap he then catalogued it as anomaly #11 of 22 — the alignment with the anti-tail pointing at Earth joining his chain of improbable geometric coincidences.
anomalies.official_explanation: Opposition alignments are a function of Earth's orbital motion, not of the object: every outer body passes near the Sun-Earth axis roughly once per synodic period (what was unusual here was only the very small 0.69-degree minimum phase angle). Mainstream astronomers used the same window productively — Hubble imaged 3I/ATLAS during the alignment, and coordinated photometry measured an opposition surge of about 0.2 mag with ~3-degree width and a linear phase slope of ~0.026 mag/deg, values consistent with ordinary cometary dust. Calling Earth's own viewing geometry an anomaly of the object is a category error.

anomalies.title: Methane volatility puzzle
anomalies.observation: Methane (CH4) was first detected in the coma only after perihelion — JWST/MIRI spectra on 2025 Dec 15-16 and 27 (2.20 and 2.54 au outbound) measured CH4 at 13.7% and 27% of the water production rate — despite CH4's volatility lying between CO2 and CO, both of which were detected well before perihelion (JWST/SPHEREx, Aug 2025, saw strong CO2 and CO but no CH4). Under simple sublimation ordering, CH4 should have appeared alongside them inbound.
anomalies.loeb_take: Anomaly #19 of his final 22-anomaly list (the 'Possible Bio-Signature' item): the out-of-order appearance of volatiles violates the layered-ice sublimation sequence expected for a natural comet, suggesting to Loeb that the plume chemistry may not be simple ice sublimation — he floated abiotic (deep-buried CH4) and speculative biological interpretations.
anomalies.official_explanation: Comet nuclei are heterogeneous: the JWST/MIRI team (Belyakov et al. 2026) attributes the late CH4 onset to past depletion of methane from the outermost processed layers, with the observed CH4 emerging from relatively unprocessed subsurface material once perihelion heating reached deeper layers — or to compositional heterogeneity of the nucleus combined with seasonal illumination effects. Volatile release order varies among well-studied solar-system comets, so a late CH4 onset is within natural diversity.
anomalies.loeb_quote: The volatility of methane (CH4) is between that of carbon dioxide (CO2) and carbon monoxide (CO), yet methane was detected in the gas plume around 3I/ATLAS only after perihelion, while CO2 and CO were detected long before perihelion.

(1) Date: announcement was 2026-01-29 (Belyakov et al., 'The Volatile Inventory of 3I/ATLAS as seen with JWST/MIRI', arXiv:2601.22034), with Loeb's Medium response on 2026-01-30; entry's 2026-01-20 was 9 days early (within the 2-week tolerance but corrected to the real date). Observations themselves were JWST/MIRI on 2025 Dec 15-16 and 27 at 2.20 and 2.54 au; CH4 measured at 13.7% and 27% of the water production rate across the two epochs; Aug 2025 JWST/SPHEREx pre-perihelion data showed no CH4 despite strong CO2 and detected CO. Nothing fabricated or conflated with another anomaly.

anomalies.title: Three symmetric mini-jets at 120 degrees
anomalies.observation: Larson-Sekanina rotational-gradient filtering of Hubble Space Telescope images (key frames 2026-01-14; pattern persistent in frames from Nov 30, Dec 4, 12, 27, 2025 and Jan 7, 2026) removed the circular coma glow and revealed three mini-jets around the nucleus separated from each other by approximately 120 degrees in sky projection, plus a fourth prominent sunward anti-tail jet extending about 10 times farther. Loeb reported the jet structure wobbles by +/-20 degrees with a 7.1-hour period.
anomalies.loeb_take: Anomaly #13 of the final 22: Loeb highlighted the engineered look of three jets 'symmetrically separated by 120 degrees' from each other, noting none points anti-sunward as a normal tail would, and on 2026-04-16 published an essay (with Toni Scarmato) linking this three-jet system to the measured non-gravitational acceleration via rocket-effect thrust — discussing whether the jets are 'technological thrusters or pockets of ice' and citing a proposed 3+1-thruster configuration as an optimal steering architecture.
anomalies.official_explanation: Multiple discrete vents are common on comet nuclei (Rosetta imaged dozens on 67P), and apparent regular spacing is a projection and small-number effect: with three jets, some near-symmetric arrangement is unremarkable. Jet-driven torques and acceleration from asymmetric outgassing are standard comet dynamics.

anomalies.title: Sideways (non-radial) non-gravitational acceleration
anomalies.observation: A February 2026 reanalysis of the orbit fits (Spada, Krolikowska & Dones, arXiv:2603.00782) showed the non-gravitational acceleration was not purely directed away from the Sun (as rocket-effect sublimation predicts to first order): Loeb highlighted that the tangential component was comparable in magnitude to the radial one, whereas NASA/JPL's fit had the radial component about 5x the tangential — itself well above the ~0.03-0.05 transverse-to-radial ratio typical of solar-system comets.

The mainstream rebuttal (Spada et al. 2026) is that the fitted transverse component A2 is the least stable parameter — highly sensitive to data selection, parameter correlations, and orbital phase coverage — while total acceleration estimates agree with JPL's solution and require no exotic physics.

anomalies.title: Anomalous isotope abundances (D/H, 12C/13C, 14N/15N)
anomalies.observation: JWST (Cordiner et al.) reported deuterium-enriched water with D/H more than ten times higher than known comets, and 12C/13C of 141-191 (CO2) and 123-172 (CO), above typical solar-system values; VLT (Opitom et al.) found 12C/13C = 147 (+87/-40) and 14N/15N = 343 (+454/-124), over twice the ~150 typical of solar-system comets.
anomalies.loeb_take: In 'New Anomalies in the Isotope Abundances of 3I/ATLAS' (Mar 10, 2026) Loeb accepted the papers' inference of formation below 30 K in a metal-poor environment 10-12 billion years ago, but argued that ancient low-metallicity stellar populations cannot supply enough rocky material — they 'miss the required mass budget by at least three orders of magnitude'. The same day he reduced 3I/ATLAS to rank 3 on the Loeb scale, conditional on an uneventful Jupiter pass.
anomalies.official_explanation: The measuring teams interpret the isotopes as strong evidence for a natural, extremely ancient comet formed at freezing temperatures early in the Milky Way's history — the isotopic signature of great age, not technology. The mass-budget objection depends on Loeb's contested large-mass estimate; for a km-scale nucleus no reservoir problem arises.

events.title: TESS pre-discovery detections begin
events.description: NASA's TESS spacecraft serendipitously imaged 3I/ATLAS from 2025-05-07 to 2025-06-02, 55 days before discovery, at roughly 6.4 AU from the Sun. Precovery photometry suggests the object was already active at ~6 AU, implying sublimation of ices more volatile than water.

events.title: Earliest ZTF precovery images
events.description: Zwicky Transient Facility precovery detections date back to 2025-05-22 (identified on individual unstacked images by Seligman et al.), with additional detection runs 2025-06-14 to 2025-06-21 and 2025-06-22 to 2025-06-29 identified within hours of the discovery report. ATLAS's own archives held precoveries from 2025-06-05 to 2025-06-29.

events.title: Vera C. Rubin Observatory serendipitous imaging
events.description: The Rubin Observatory captured 3I/ATLAS by chance during science-validation imaging starting 2025-06-21, ten days before discovery — among the highest-quality early data on the object.

events.title: Discovery by ATLAS, Rio Hurtado, Chile
events.description: The ATLAS survey telescope at Rio Hurtado, Chile (station W68) discovered the object at apparent magnitude ~18, 4.51 AU from the Sun and 3.50 AU from Earth, inbound at ~61 km/s relative to the Sun.

events.title: Confirmed interstellar — designated 3I/ATLAS (C/2025 N1)
events.description: Follow-up astrometry confirmed a strongly hyperbolic orbit (eccentricity 6.141, hyperbolic excess velocity ~58 km/s — faster than 1I/'Oumuamua at 26 km/s and 2I/Borisov at 32 km/s). The Minor Planet Center announced it as the third confirmed interstellar object; Nordic Optical Telescope and Teide Observatory confirmed cometary activity the same day.

events.title: Loeb raises 'alien technology' hypothesis; anomaly list begins
events.description: Avi Loeb (with Adam Hibberd and Adam Crowl) posted the arXiv paper 'Is the Interstellar Object 3I/ATLAS Alien Technology?' (arXiv:2507.12213, v1 2025-07-16), starting a running numbered list of anomalies (retrograde ecliptic-aligned trajectory ~0.2% probability, fine-tuned Mars/Jupiter arrival geometry, etc.) that grew to 22 items by March 2026. NASA/ESA and most astronomers maintained it is a natural comet throughout.

events.title: Hubble images constrain nucleus size
events.description: Hubble Space Telescope imaging constrained the nucleus diameter to 0.32-5.6 km and revealed a sunward dust fan / anti-solar tail. Later non-gravitational-acceleration analyses pointed to a sub-kilometer nucleus — roughly 0.8-1.1 km diameter and mass ~1.6e11 kg if the acceleration is driven by CO2 outgassing (Thoss, Loeb & Burkert).

events.title: JWST: unusually CO2-rich composition
events.description: JWST NIRSpec observations (results announced 2025-08-25) found a coma unusually rich in carbon dioxide — CO2/H2O mixing ratio 8.0±1.0, among the highest ever measured — with CO2 at 129±1 kg/s, water 6.6±0.2 kg/s, CO 14.0±0.9 kg/s, plus water ice and carbonyl sulfide.

events.title: SPHEREx maps giant CO2 coma; VLT confirms cyanide and nickel
events.description: NASA's SPHEREx (observing 2025-08-08 to 08-12) reported a CO2 gas coma spanning at least 348,000 km in radius (~70 kg/s CO2) plus water ice. Concurrent VLT spectroscopy confirmed cyanide (17.6±2.0 g/s) alongside atomic nickel (4.6±0.7 g/s, first detected 2025-07-20) with no accompanying iron vapor — the nickel-without-iron signature became Loeb anomaly material, though nickel-carbonyl chemistry in normal comets can explain it.

events.title: Mars close approach — 0.194 AU; imaged by Mars orbiters
events.description: 3I/ATLAS passed 0.194 AU (29.0 million km) from Mars at 04:38 UT. NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter HiRISE imaged it at ~30 km/pixel (a diffuse, comet-consistent smear), ESA's ExoMars TGO CaSSIS captured the coma in 5-second exposures, and MAVEN detected hydrogen in the UV. HiRISE image release was delayed ~6 weeks by the US government shutdown.

events.title: Solar conjunction — unobservable from Earth
events.description: The comet passed behind the Sun as seen from Earth around 2025-10-21, making its perihelion unobservable from the ground; Earth-based observers lost it for roughly late October through early November 2025 (solar elongation under ~25 deg from 2025-10-04 to 2025-11-06). Spacecraft (including GOES-19 and Mars/solar assets) provided partial coverage.

events.title: Perihelion — 1.36 AU from the Sun
events.description: Perihelion at 11:45 UT on 2025-10-29 at 1.356 AU (203 million km), between the orbits of Earth and Mars, moving at its maximum speed of ~68 km/s. It brightened faster near perihelion than typical comets — item 22 on Loeb's anomaly list, attributed by most astronomers to hypervolatile-driven outgassing.

events.title: Post-conjunction reemergence in the morning sky
events.description: Ground-based observers recovered the comet after solar conjunction; astrophotographer Michael Jaeger imaged the revived dust tail on 2025-11-08. Post-perihelion astrometry soon showed non-gravitational acceleration peaking at (89.3±4.6)e-9 AU/day^2 about a month before perihelion — normal for a small actively-outgassing nucleus, but logged by Loeb as an anomaly for its sideways component.

events.title: NASA press event: 'it's a comet' — HiRISE, MAVEN, Hubble, JWST data released
events.description: After the government shutdown ended, NASA held a live press event releasing spacecraft imagery (HiRISE at 30 km/pixel, MAVEN UV hydrogen detection, Hubble, JWST, SPHEREx) and stating 3I/ATLAS 'exhibits behaviors typical of comets' — gas and dust shedding, gravitational response — i.e., a natural comet. Loeb publicly criticized the conference for dismissing his anomalies. ESA's JUICE spacecraft also observed the comet during November 2025 en route to Jupiter.

events.title: Earth closest approach — 1.80 AU
events.description: Closest approach to Earth at 06:01 UT on 2025-12-19 at 1.798 AU (269 million km), out beyond the 4:1 Kirkwood gap of the asteroid belt, at apparent magnitude ~19.9 — never any threat to Earth. Around the same period a second JWST epoch detected methane that had been absent pre-perihelion.

events.title: Radio technosignature searches come up empty (ATA + MeerKAT)
events.description: A SETI Institute / Allen Telescope Array search (Sheikh et al., arXiv:2512.18142, submitted 2025-12-19) scanned 1-9 GHz for 7.25 hours around the Earth close approach: ~74 million narrowband hits reduced to 211 candidates by RFI filtering, all rejected — no technosignatures, with EIRP upper limits of ~10-110 W across the band. An earlier MeerKAT search (900-1670 MHz) had likewise found nothing, with a minimum EIRP limit of ~0.17 W (below cellphone-handset power).

events.title: Opposition — best final viewing geometry
events.description: 3I/ATLAS reached opposition at 177.6 deg solar elongation, visible all night but fading; Loeb separately flagged the 2026-01-22 alignment with the Sun-Earth axis to within 0.69 deg (phase angle under 2 deg for about a week) as a rare chance to measure the opposition surge of its dust. Large telescopes continued photometric monitoring of the outbound comet.

events.title: Loeb publishes final tally of 22 anomalies
events.description: As the comet faded, Loeb's Medium essay enumerated 22 anomalies across mass/geometry, jet behavior, composition (nickel>iron, unusual isotopes), and trajectory coincidences (including a claimed 0.6%-probability alignment within 9 deg of the 1977 'Wow! Signal' arrival direction), ranking it Level 4 on his own 'Loeb Scale.' Mainstream rebuttals (e.g., Penn State's AstroWright) argued each item is explicable for a natural comet.

events.title: Jupiter close approach — 0.358 AU; Juno stays home
events.description: Closest approach to Jupiter at 12:22 UT at 0.358 AU (53.6 million km); it also passed 0.204 AU from the small Jovian moon Eupheme on 2026-03-17. A proposed Juno intercept (Loeb/Hibberd, arXiv:2507.21402 — requiring a ~2.7 km/s burn in September 2025) was never executed: Juno was low on fuel with engine problems and was not redirected; no Juno flyby observations resulted.

events.title: ESA JUICE results: an ordinary comet seen from close range
events.description: ESA released JUICE observations taken in November 2025, days after perihelion, from ~60 million km (JANUS camera and NavCam plus the MAJIS, SWI, and UVS spectrometers): a distinct coma with gas and dust extending over 5 million km, separate dust and anti-solar tails, and water output of ~2,000 kg/s on 2025-11-02 — equivalent to ~70 Olympic swimming pools per day, mostly from the sunward side — all consistent with a normal, if volatile-rich, comet.

events.title: Loeb status essay: a fading dot at 6.7 AU
events.description: Loeb's 'Where is 3I/ATLAS Now?' put the comet at ~1 billion km (6.7 AU) from the Sun, well beyond Jupiter, 'heading away from us back to interstellar space' and nearing the detectability horizon; he reorganized his claims into 12 anomaly categories at 'Loeb Scale' Level 4, while conceding the object is leaving without any close inspection.

events.title: Second solar conjunction — ground observability ends
events.description: Around May 2026 (date approximate) 3I/ATLAS entered its second solar conjunction, ending routine ground-based observation. When it reemerges around September 2026 it will be beyond Saturn's orbit and fainter than magnitude 20 — effectively the end of its observable apparition for all but the largest telescopes.

events.title: Published ATA study reaffirms: no signals
events.description: The peer-reviewed Allen Telescope Array result (published in The Astronomical Journal, revised May 2026) circulated widely in June 2026 (date approximate): a seven-hour, 1-9 GHz scan found no technosignatures from 3I/ATLAS, closing out the SETI angle as the object receded. Loeb continued essays into June 2026 (e.g., on dust 'windshield' effects) but no new observational anomalies emerged.

events.title: Current status: nearing Saturn's orbital distance, outbound for good
events.description: As of today 3I/ATLAS is about 9.25 AU from the Sun (~1.38 billion km; 10.25 AU from Earth per JPL Horizons), reaching Saturn's ~9.5 AU orbital distance in late July while hidden in solar conjunction (solar elongation ~9 deg) — unobservable and fainter than magnitude 20. It is escaping on its hyperbolic trajectory at ~58 km/s excess velocity, nearly symmetric to its inbound path; it will pass the inner Oort cloud region (~2,000 AU) around the year 2189 and leave the Sun's influence entirely in a few thousand years. Consensus verdict: the most-studied interstellar object ever, and a natural — though unusually CO2-rich, nickel-emitting, and ancient (possibly 7-14 billion years old) — comet.

objects.name: 'Oumuamua
objects.discovered: 2017-10-19, Pan-STARRS1 (Haleakala, Hawaii) — found ~40 days after perihelion, on the way out
objects.size_estimate: ~100-400 m long (est. 100-1,000 m range), width/thickness ~35-167 m; extreme axis ratio ~6:1 to 10:1 (cigar or pancake shape)
objects.nature: Inert/rocky-appearing; no detected coma, dust, or gas despite deep searches — yet accelerated like a comet. Composition still debated (nitrogen ice, hydrogen ice, dark organic-rich crust all proposed)
weird_notes: Non-gravitational acceleration (~5x10^-6 m/s^2 at 1 AU, radial ~2.8x10^-7 AU/d^2) with NO visible outgassing — no coma, no dust, no detected gas to explain it
Extreme lightcurve amplitude ~2.5 magnitudes implying axis ratio of at least 6:1, more elongated than any known solar-system asteroid or comet
Tumbling (non-principal-axis) rotation, period ~7.3-8 h
Red, comet-like surface color but zero cometary activity detected by Spitzer and deep ground-based imaging
Excess velocity vector close to the Local Standard of Rest — dynamically 'young' / unusual for an ejected planetesimal
Only detected post-perihelion at close range; observed arc was short (~2.5 months), so many properties remain unresolved
objects.loeb_position: Loeb (Bialy & Loeb 2018, ApJL) argued the non-gravitational acceleration without outgassing could be explained by solar radiation pressure on a thin, flat artificial object — a lightsail or discarded 'technological debris' from an alien civilization. He expanded this in his 2021 book 'Extraterrestrial,' maintaining the artificial-origin hypothesis is more plausible than exotic natural explanations like hydrogen icebergs.

objects.name: Borisov
objects.discovered: 2019-08-30, Gennadiy Borisov (amateur astronomer), 0.65-m MARGO observatory, Nauchnij, Crimea
objects.size_estimate: Nucleus effective radius 0.2-0.5 km (HST); early ~975 m estimates were revised down. Coma/tail much larger (tail ~160,000 km)
objects.nature: Clearly cometary from first detection — bright coma and tail, normal dust and gas production. The 'ordinary' interstellar object; behaved like a moderately active solar-system comet
weird_notes: Extremely CO-rich: CO/H2O ratio 3x+ higher than any comet measured in the inner solar system, suggesting formation beyond the CO ice line of a cold M-dwarf or outer disk (Bodewits et al. / Cordiner et al. 2020)
NH2-rich chemistry relative to typical comets
Unusually pristine dust — suggested it had never before passed close to any star
Nucleus fragmented/split in March 2020 after an outburst, post-perihelion (a normal thing for comets to do, but notable)
Otherwise the control case: proved interstellar comets can look exactly like ordinary comets
objects.loeb_position: Loeb accepted Borisov as a genuine natural comet and repeatedly uses it as his control case: 'Borisov looked like a comet from day one, which shows astronomers can recognize a comet when they see one — making 'Oumuamua's weirdness stand out.' He noted its pristine condition was mildly interesting but did not claim artificiality.

objects.name: ATLAS
objects.discovered: 2025-07-01, ATLAS survey telescope, Rio Hurtado, Chile (prediscovery images: ATLAS back to 2025-06-05, ZTF to 2025-06-14; TESS imagery from May 2025 recovered later)
objects.perihelion_date: 2025-10-29 (11:45 UT); perihelion occurred behind the Sun as seen from Earth
objects.size_estimate: Nucleus diameter 0.32-5.6 km (HST upper/lower bounds); non-gravitational-acceleration-based estimate ~0.82-1.05 km diameter (Forbes & Butler 2025, for density 0.5 g/cm^3); Loeb et al.'s pre-perihelion NGA upper limit instead implied a MINIMUM mass ~33 billion metric tons (3.3x10^13 kg) and diameter >~5 km — the two are in tension; rotation period 16.16 h
objects.nature: Active comet, CO2-dominated: JWST/NIRSpec (2025-08-06, 3.32 AU) measured CO2/H2O mixing ratio 7.6+/-0.3 (exceptionally high, 4.5-sigma above the comet trend), Q(CO2) 9.5x10^26 molecules/s (~70 kg/s) vs Q(H2O) 1.07x10^26 (~3 kg/s) pre-perihelion; also CO, carbonyl sulfide, water ice, later methane, plus nickel vapor. Likely an old, thick-crusted comet from the Milky Way thick disk. NASA/ESA and mainstream astronomy: natural comet
weird_notes: Most eccentric orbit ever recorded for a solar-system-passing object: e = 6.14135 +/- 0.00002 (vs 1.2 for 1I, 3.36 for 2I) — v_inf ~58 km/s, faster than both predecessors
Retrograde orbit inclined only ~5 deg from the ecliptic plane (i = 175.12 deg) — Loeb puts chance alignment at ~0.2%
Trajectory threaded close to Mars (0.19 AU, 2025-10-03), Venus, and Jupiter (0.357 AU, 2026-03-16) while unobservable from Earth at perihelion
CO2/H2O ratio ~8 (7.6+/-0.3, JWST) — among the highest ever measured in any comet
Nickel-rich gas plume with anomalously low iron and Ni/CN ratio orders of magnitude above known comets (detected Aug 2025, VLT/UVES; Ni production ~0.9 g/s rising to ~5 g/s by 2.8 AU)
Pre-perihelion sunward anti-tail/collimated jet, later roughly symmetric jets post-perihelion; reported mini-jets separated ~120 deg
Non-gravitational acceleration detected at perihelion with a substantial non-radial (sideways) component (per Loeb's analysis of MPC/JPL astrometry)
Extreme negative polarization reported as unprecedented among known comets; near perihelion it brightened faster than known comets and appeared bluer than the Sun

Post-perihelion chemistry shift: methane emerged as ices faded — first CH4 detection on an interstellar object (Belyakov et al. 2026, ApJL, JWST/MIRI, Dec 2025 obs): CH4/H2O mixing ratio 11.0+/-0.5% rising to 21.6+/-1.3%, vs 0.1-10% for typical solar-system comets; separate June 2026 Nature paper (Cordiner et al., JWST isotopes: 12C/13C = 147, 14N/15N = 343) points to a cold, distant birth environment
Big and fast: nucleus estimated 3-5 orders of magnitude more massive than both 1I and 2I (Loeb: 'at least 100,000x Oumuamua'), in tension with expected interstellar-object mass distribution

Jupiter flyby 2026-03-16 at 0.357 AU passed as predicted on the gravitational trajectory (perijove 53.445 Mkm ~ Jupiter's Hill radius 53.502 Mkm — Loeb anomaly); ESA's Juice spacecraft (MAJIS, obs 2025-11-02, published 2026-04-02) measured water output ~2,000 kg/s (~70 Olympic pools/day) and a tail ~6 million km long
Status July 2026: outbound beyond Jupiter's distance in Gemini, magnitude ~15 and fading, leaving the solar system permanently (beyond Saturn's orbit and fainter than mag 20 by ~Sept 2026)
objects.loeb_position: Loeb maintained a running numbered anomaly file (reaching 22 anomalies by his March 2026 Medium summary '3I/ATLAS is Fading Away...'), assigning individual probabilities to coincidences (perijove ~ Jupiter's Hill radius, Wow! Signal alignment within 9 deg at 0.6% probability, ecliptic alignment, jet geometry). He rated it 4 on his 0-10 'Loeb scale' (10 = alien threat) — anomalous enough to warrant the technological hypothesis but 'slightly less anomalous' than 'Oumuamua — and repeatedly urged agencies to collect more data rather than dismiss the possibility; NASA/ESA and nearly all astronomers concluded it is a natural, unusually CO2-rich interstellar comet.

quotes.text: As of now, I assign a 30 to 40 percent likelihood that 3I/ATLAS does not have a fully natural origin
quotes.speaker: Avi Loeb
quotes.context: Probability estimate of non-natural origin, as reported while anomaly count grew
quotes.source: Futurism (futurism.com/space/astronomer-probability-alien-craft-comet)

quotes.text: This low-probability scenario includes the possibility of a black swan event akin to a Trojan Horse, where a technological object masquerades as a natural comet.
quotes.speaker: Avi Loeb
quotes.context: Explaining his 'black swan' framing of the technological hypothesis
quotes.source: Futurism, quoting Loeb's Medium blog

quotes.text: As far as I know, there are no protocols for responding to the discovery of functioning alien devices near Earth.
quotes.speaker: Avi Loeb
quotes.context: On planetary preparedness if 3I/ATLAS proved technological
quotes.source: Futurism, quoting Loeb

quotes.text: As largely a pedagogical exercise, in this paper we present additional analysis into the astrodynamics of 3I/ATLAS, and hypothesize that this object could be technological
quotes.speaker: Avi Loeb (with Adam Hibberd, Adam Crowl)
quotes.context: Abstract of the paper 'Is the Interstellar Object 3I/ATLAS Alien Technology?'

quotes.text: possibly hostile as would be expected from the 'Dark Forest' resolution to the 'Fermi Paradox'
quotes.speaker: Avi Loeb (with Adam Hibberd, Adam Crowl)
quotes.context: The 'dark forest' line in the same arXiv paper's abstract

quotes.text: If it is technological — it may maneuver to benefit from the Sun's gravitational assist or release probes that could intercept the Earth or other planets owing to its retrograde orbit.
quotes.speaker: Avi Loeb
quotes.context: Warning about the perihelion pass hidden behind the Sun, in his Mars-flyby anomaly recap
quotes.source: Avi Loeb, Medium (A Recap of the Anomalies of 3I/ATLAS on the Day of Its Closest Approach to Mars)

quotes.text: If we find technological satellites of Jupiter that we did not send, it would imply that Jupiter is of interest to an extraterrestrial civilization.
quotes.speaker: Avi Loeb
quotes.context: On the March 16, 2026 Jupiter approach at ~Jupiter's Hill radius and the idea of released 'devices'
quotes.source: Avi Loeb, Medium (Jupiter-approach essays); IBTimes UK coverage

quotes.text: NASA's representatives should have emphasized what we do not understand about 3I/ATLAS rather than insist that it is a familiar comet from a new birth environment.
quotes.speaker: Avi Loeb
quotes.context: Reaction to NASA's post-shutdown press conference
quotes.source: Avi Loeb, Medium (There is Nothing More Deceptive than an Obvious Fact)

quotes.text: We should be humble about the little we know and curious about 3I/ATLAS rather than insist that we know its nature before data is shared and analyzed.
quotes.speaker: Avi Loeb
quotes.context: Essay inviting Kim Kardashian to join his research team, criticizing NASA data withholding
quotes.source: Avi Loeb, Medium (Kim Kardashian is Welcome to Join my Research Team on 3I/ATLAS)

quotes.text: Scientific truth is not decided by authority or popularity but by attention to data.
quotes.speaker: Avi Loeb
quotes.context: Response to astronomers insisting 3I/ATLAS is a natural comet
quotes.source: Newsweek interview

quotes.text: It is the responsibility of scientists and NASA officials to acknowledge the existence of unexplained puzzles rather than display the arrogance of expertise while ignoring them.
quotes.speaker: Avi Loeb
quotes.context: Farewell essay as the object faded, tallying 22 anomalies and lowering it to Loeb Scale 3
quotes.source: Avi Loeb, Medium (3I/ATLAS is Fading Away, Leaving Us to Ponder Over Its 22 Mysterious Anomalies)

quotes.text: Given how well aligned its trajectory was with the orbital plane of Earth around the Sun, we might never witness a visitor like it in our lifetime.
quotes.speaker: Avi Loeb
quotes.context: Status essay with 3I/ATLAS a billion km out, well beyond Jupiter, leaving the solar system
quotes.source: Avi Loeb, Medium (Where is 3I/ATLAS Now?)

quotes.text: This object is a comet. It looks and behaves like a comet, and all evidence points to it being a comet.
quotes.speaker: Amit Kshatriya, NASA Associate Administrator
quotes.context: NASA press conference releasing post-shutdown 3I/ATLAS imagery
quotes.source: NASA live event; LiveNOW from FOX / Space.com coverage

quotes.text: We very much want to find signs of life in our universe... but 3I/ATLAS is a comet.
quotes.speaker: Amit Kshatriya, NASA Associate Administrator
quotes.context: Same NASA press conference, addressing alien-technology speculation directly
quotes.source: NASA press conference; LiveNOW from FOX coverage

quotes.text: Everybody has got a camera and they're trying to get a picture of the ball. Nobody has the perfect view, and everybody has a different camera.
quotes.speaker: Tom Statler, NASA lead scientist for solar system small bodies
quotes.context: Baseball-stadium analogy for the multi-spacecraft observation campaign at the NASA press conference
quotes.source: NASA press conference; Space.com coverage

quotes.speaker: Sean Duffy, NASA Acting Administrator

timelineVerify.corrections: Five entries corrected; all other 18 confirmed against primary sources. (1) 2026-04-02 JUICE entry: observations were NOT taken "around the Jupiter approach" — ESA's 2026-04-02 release covers observations made in November 2025, days after perihelion, from ~60 million km (MAJIS measured 2000 kg/s of water on 2025-11-02 = ~70 Olympic pools/day); instruments were the JANUS camera plus MAJIS/SWI/UVS spectrometers and NavCam; gas and dust extended >5 million km. Loeb Medium source replaced with the actual ESA release. (2) 2025-07-21 Hubble entry: the claimed later size estimate "~0.52-0.75 km, mass ~4.4e10 kg" is unsupported by any located paper; actual non-gravitational-acceleration analyses (arXiv:2512.18341; Thoss, Loeb & Burkert arXiv:2603.15735) give ~0.42 km radius (~0.84 km diameter, or 0.82-1.05 km with time-lag solutions) and mass ~1.6e11 kg for CO2-dominated outgassing. (3) 2025-08-21 entry: VLT first detected atomic nickel on 2025-07-20, weeks before the 2025-08-21 cyanide confirmation (dataset implied both were detected the same day); SPHEREx observations were 2025-08-08 to 08-12 with results posted ~Aug 21 (arXiv:2508.15469, CO2 mass loss ~70 kg/s). (4) ATA radio-search entry: date tightened from 2025-12-22 to 2025-12-19 (arXiv:2512.18142 v1 submission, Sheikh et al.); the ATA search's own EIRP upper limit is 10-110 W — the 0.17 W figure is MeerKAT's minimum EIRP (900-1670 MHz), which the dataset had right but is now stated unambiguously. Paper later published in The Astronomical Journal (revised 2026-05-20), consistent with the June 2026 publicity entry. (5) 2026-07-17 current-status entry: JPL Horizons gives r = 9.25 AU (1.38 billion km) from the Sun and 10.25 AU from Earth on 2026-07-17, solar elongation 8.9 deg (deep in conjunction, confirmed), receding at ~58.8 km/s — corrected from "roughly 9.5 AU (~1.4 billion km)"; it crosses Saturn's ~9.54 AU orbital distance in late July 2026, so "crossing Saturn's orbital distance this month" stands. Minor: ZTF entry's later detection run corrected from "2025-06-28/29" to 2025-06-22 to 06-29 (per Wikipedia's precovery table); earliest ZTF precovery 2025-05-22 confirmed via Seligman et al. Everything else verified exact: discovery 2025-07-01 (W68, mag 18, 4.51 AU, 61 km/s); e=6.14135 and MPC confirmation 2025-07-02; Loeb arXiv:2507.12213 v1 2025-07-16; TESS 2025-05-07 to 06-02 (arXiv:2508.02499); JWST 2025-08-06, CO2/H2O 8.0+/-1.0; Mars 2025-10-03 0.1937 AU; conjunction 2025-10-21; perihelion 2025-10-29 11:45 UT, 1.3564 AU, 68 km/s; non-grav accel (89.3+/-4.6)e-9 AU/day^2; NASA event 2025-11-19; Earth approach 2025-12-19 06:01 UT, 1.7976 AU; Dec methane; opposition 2026-01-22 at 177.6 deg with 0.69-deg Sun-Earth-axis alignment (arXiv:2601.08624); Loeb 22-anomalies essay published 2026-03-12 (Wow-signal 0.6%, Loeb Scale Level 4 confirmed); Jupiter approach 2026-03-16 12:22 UT, 0.3583 AU; Eupheme 0.2036 AU on 2026-03-17; Juno intercept paper arXiv:2507.21402 (~2.7 km/s burn, never executed); Loeb "Where is 3I/ATLAS Now?" published 2026-04-23 (6.7 AU, 12 anomaly categories); second solar conjunction ~May 2026 with September 2026 reemergence beyond Saturn's orbit fainter than mag 20.

comparisonVerify.corrections: 1I and 2I entries: fully confirmed against JPL SBDB/MPC (no changes). 3I/ATLAS entry corrected on 7 points: (1) Methane result misattributed — it is Belyakov et al., ApJL (JWST/MIRI, Dec 2025 observations at 2.20-2.54 AU, DOI 10.3847/2041-8213/ae5700, announced Apr-Jun 2026), NOT the June 2026 Nature Cordiner/NIRSpec paper; the '~11x higher than any solar-system object' claim is a garbling of the measured CH4:H2O mixing ratio of 11.0+/-0.5% (rising to 21.6+/-1.3% at the second epoch) vs 0.1-10% for typical comets (C/2016 R2 is higher at 181%). The June 2026 Nature paper (Cordiner et al., 'Isotopic evidence for a cold and distant origin of 3I/ATLAS') is the ISOTOPE study: 12C/13C = 147(+87/-40), 14N/15N = 343 (>2x solar-system comets). (2) JWST CO2/H2O mixing ratio: published ApJL value is 7.6+/-0.3 (8.0+/-1.0 was the early preprint value); production rates at 3.32 AU were Q(CO2)=9.5e26 molecules/s (~70 kg/s) and Q(H2O)=1.07e26 molecules/s (~3 kg/s), not 129 and 6.6 kg/s. (3) Non-gravitational-acceleration-based nucleus size is 0.82-1.05 km (Forbes & Butler, arXiv 2512.18341), not 0.44-0.75 km; the 'mass ~4.4e10 kg' figure is unsupported — the published mass claim is Loeb et al.'s MINIMUM ~33 billion metric tons (3.3e13 kg, implying diameter >~5 km) derived from the pre-perihelion NGA upper limit (arXiv 2509.21408), in tension with the ~1 km post-perihelion NGA estimate. (4) Mass-ratio anomaly: published claim is 3-5 orders of magnitude more massive than both 1I and 2I (Loeb: 'at least a hundred thousand times that of Oumuamua'), not 10^6x vs 1I and 10^3x vs 2I. (5) The April 2026 ESA results came from the Juice spacecraft (MAJIS instrument, observations 2025-11-02, four days post-perihelion, published 2026-04-02): water ~2,000 kg/s = ~70 Olympic pools/day (confirmed) but ion tail ~6 million km long (gas/dust envelope >5 million km) — not 'tail ~5 million km'. (6) Nickel production: reported ~0.9 g/s (Aug 2025, VLT/UVES) rising to ~5 g/s at 2.8 AU; replaced flat '4.6 g/s'. (7) Prediscovery detail expanded: ATLAS images to 2025-06-05, ZTF to 2025-06-14, with TESS imagery from May 2025 recovered later (JPL orbit fits use observations back to late May 2025). All other 3I values verified correct: e=6.14135+/-0.00002, i=175.12 deg (4.89 deg from ecliptic plane, retrograde), q=1.35645 AU, perihelion 2025-10-29 11:45 UT, Earth closest 1.80 AU on 2025-12-19, Mars 0.19 AU on 2025-10-03, Jupiter 0.357 AU on 2026-03-16 (perijove 53.445 Mkm ~ Jupiter Hill radius 53.502 Mkm), v_inf 58 km/s, rotation 16.16 h, HST diameter bounds 0.32-5.6 km, Loeb's 22 anomalies (March 2026 'Fading Away' essay), Loeb scale rating 4 (unchanged as of Dec 2025 update essay), 'slightly less anomalous than Oumuamua' (Loeb's exact framing), Wow! Signal alignment within 9 deg (Loeb probability 0.6%), July 2026 status (outbound beyond Jupiter's distance, constellation Gemini, magnitude ~15 and fading, beyond Saturn's orbit and mag >20 by ~Sept 2026).
